summary: Pipelined stream crosstalk causing gradual 'throughput staircase' and transient GPU starvation in dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: BrightLens reports a gradual, stepwise degradation in sustained throughput for their dedicated pool during midday traffic. Pattern described as a 'throughput staircase' where p50 stays steady but p95/p99 and overall steady-state throughput drop in discrete steps over ~30-90 minutes. Impact: customer-facing inference latency increases, queued requests, and periodic fallback to lower-capacity model variants. Environment: prod dedicated pool (us-east) serving redwood-3b-v1 for BrightLens route. Timeline: 2026-03-10 11:05 first alert from customer; 11:12 automated SLO alert p99 > 1200ms; 11:30 autoscaler triggered a scale-up for the pool; 11:45 throughput dropped further despite new GPUs attaching. Observed behaviour: GPUs appear healthy but effective slot utilization falls on a subset of GPUs; some GPUs show near-zero active streams while others are saturated. Hypothesis: pipelined stream crosstalk — an ordering/contention pathology where short, high-priority streams serialize long batched pipelines on certain GPUs due to affinity and batcher placement, causing incremental GPU detachment and autoscaler misread (interpreting serialized GPUs as underutilized) which drives corrective (but delayed) autoscaler actions, producing a staircase-like throughput decline. This exhibits features different from simple noisy-tenant hogging: streams are partially serialized by pipeline ordering and internal prefetch/eviction timing which causes transient per-GPU starvation rather than uniform noise across tenants.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a small dedicated pool (4 GPUs) and route mixed short-low-latency streams and long batched streams from two tenants.
2) Configure batcher with adaptive batching + KV cache and enable pipeline prefetcher in the serving-runtime.
3) Generate a steady long-batched workload (simulating BrightLens long context runs) and interleave microbursts of short streams from a second tenant every ~15s.
4) Observe throughput, per-GPU active stream counts, and autoscaler decisions for 1 hour; look for stepwise throughput decline and GPU slot skew.
Notes: reproducer workload attached in related_github_prs gh#4521.
logs: [11:33:18] autoscaler: attach_request accepted -> attaching 1 GPU (reason: measured_queue_sleep > threshold)
[11:42:50] batcher: eviction event for KV cache on gpu-2 (evict_count=128) -> pipeline serializing short streams
Stacktrace snippet: serving-runtime: batcher.cpp:412 handle_prefetch() -> wait_for_pipeline_lock() -> 0x7fffa3b2
comments: Leah Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reports gradual throughput drops in dedicated pool; provided example timestamps and route names. Asked for diagnostics and whether any recent rollout could cause this.

Marcus Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-10: Picked up ticket, started collecting per-GPU stream histograms and batcher logs. Noted uneven active_stream distribution. Added to oncall channel #support and flagged as P1.
BrightLens Ops (customer) 2026-03-10: We're seeing increased tail latency and periodic queueing that recovers slowly; can provide replay traces if needed.

Marcus Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-11: Correlated autoscaler attach events with evictions. Hypothesis: pipeline ordering + short-stream fanout serializing long pipelines. Requesting reproduction guidance for engineering.
Iris Nguyen (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-12: Reproduced locally with adaptive batcher + prefetcher enabled. Opening PRs to add per-GPU pipeline-lock metrics (gh#4538).
investigation_notes: Collected per-GPU telemetry from 11:00-12:30: stream_count variance high (stdev up to 7.4 across GPUs) during incident window.
KV cache eviction spikes align with the start of each 'stair' in throughput decline.
Autoscaler judged some GPUs as underutilized (active_streams near 0) and queued detachment on shrink windows, but GPUs were actually serialized and unable to accept new batches due to pipeline locks.
No driver-level errors or OOMs observed. NVLink and PCIe latencies within baseline.
Reproducer confirms that inserting short-high-priority streams every 10-20s increases serialization and leads to stepwise throughput drop in 30-90 minute window.
Added temporary instrumentation points: pipeline_lock_wait_ms, per_gpu_batch_queue_depth; data attached to confluence page.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied 2026-03-12: disabled pipeline prefetcher on affected pool and tuned batcher to prefer rebalancing across GPUs (config change: batcher.max_serialization_window -> 150ms). Immediate result: throughput stabilized and stepwise decline stopped.
Short-term rollback: reverted autoscaler shrink heuristic to use active_batch_accept_rate instead of raw active_streams for underutilization signals.
Customer BrightLens notified and observed restored p99 baseline within 20 minutes of mitigation.
Engineering to land hard fix (prevent pipeline lock starvation and improve autoscaler signals) in next runtime patch (see gh#4538).
follow_up_actions: ENG: Add permanent pipeline_lock telemetry and create an alert for high per_gpu_pipeline_lock_wait_ms (owner: runtime team, ticket created gh#4538).
SRE: Update autoscaler heuristic to include batch acceptance rate and KV cache eviction rate before marking GPU underutilized (owner: autoscaler team).
DOCS: Add runbook section for 'throughput staircase' incidents describing mitigations (owner: CS/Runbooks).
Customer follow-up: schedule a 1:1 postmortem with BrightLens to review mitigations and confirm SLA remediation (owner: CS).
